answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. This mechanism ensures that only legitimate users can participate in a task. When cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, the system will slash the offending identity, like a forge burning false claims. The remaining identities will be left to glow like an ember, symbolizing their legitimacy. This approach prevents a single entity from dominating the system, like a karst landscape eroded by excessive use.
